new_problem_draft.title: Nonconvergence of randomized subtraction games with all odd moves
new_problem_draft.body:
Let $S$ be a finite nonempty set of positive odd integers. For a heap of $n$ chips let $E_n=\{k\in S:k\le n\}$. Define the probability of winning for the player to move by $a_n=0$ when $E_n$ is empty and otherwise
$$a_n=1-\frac1{|E_n|}\sum_{k\in E_n}a_{n-k}.$$
Is it true that $(a_n)$ has no real limit as $n\to\infty$ for every such $S$?

This is the general all-odd nonconvergence assertion discussed in Section 3 of Capitelli–Somma, not their separate characteristic-root simplicity Conjecture 3.3 (MathDB 363319). The linked paper supplies a proof for arbitrary finite nonempty $S$, without a gcd or root-simplicity hypothesis. This record is being added to connect that paper to its precise source question, not to claim that the root-simplicity conjecture is solved.

papers.title: Classical-mean power sums: the exact real-exponent ranges
papers.label: counterexample
papers.summary: For the arithmetic, geometric, harmonic and quadratic means A,G,H,Q of two positive inputs, the inequality A^n+G^n<=Q^n+H^n holds universally exactly when n<=0 or n>=1. The reverse holds universally exactly at n=0. This gives one complete real-exponent classification resolving the published Mestrovic–Andjic conjecture, including strict failures in its asserted interval. new_problem_draft.body:
Let $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ be positive integers with $\gcd(s_1,\ldots,s_m)=1$, and put $S=\sum_js_j$. Let $L(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$ be the least number $n\ge1$ of simple SOC inequalities representing
$$t^S\le\prod_{j=1}^m x_j^{s_j},\qquad x_j,t\ge0,$$
in Wang's Definition 3.1: introduce internal variables $y_1=t,y_2,\ldots,y_n\ge0$ and impose $y_i^2\le v_{c(i,0)}v_{c(i,1)}$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$, where $v$ lists all $x_j$ and $y_i$ and $c$ is an arbitrary input-index map. Existential projection over $y_2,\ldots,y_n$ must equal exactly the displayed feasible set.

If $S$ is odd, must $L(s_1,\ldots,s_m)\ge m$?

This is Wang's Section 7 open question (2), p.1512. The linked paper answers it affirmatively (in fact without the gcd assumption). It is different from the earlier bivariate minimum-cardinality conjecture indexed as MathDB 349081.

new_problem_draft.body:
Let $A=C([0,1],\mathbb C)$ with the supremum norm. For $a_1,a_2,a_3\in A$ set $P(w)=\prod_{j=1}^3(w-a_j)$ and define $P'(w)$ as the sum of products obtained by deleting one factor. Does there exist a finite $C\ge0$ such that, for every such split monic cubic whose critical set consists of exactly two distinct elements and every $z\in A$ with $P'(z)$ invertible, some critical element $b$ satisfies
$$\|P(z)-P(b)\|\le C\,\|P'(z)\|\,\|z-b\|?$$
